newsitem.title: UK: Physical copper still tight after spreads whipsaw.
newsitem.headline: Physical copper still tight after spreads whipsaw.

text.p: Europe's physical copper market was tight and premiums little changed on Wednesday despite the recent violent expansion and contraction of nearby LME spreads, traders said.
Physical market traders had expected premiums to ease this week after cash to three months backwardation flared out to a high of $210 on Friday.
But the sharp narrowing of the spread on Monday was too sudden to allow much metal to be attracted into the tight market, they added. Cash/threes was last at around $65 backwardation.
"There's been some tonnage coming in but I suspect that will dry up in the next few days and then you'll see some tonnage coming out again," a trader said.
LME copper stocks rose by 2,675 tonnes on Wednesday for the first time since February.
"The backwardation only built up over a few days and it disappeared just as quickly. It didn't give a chance for things to really change," another trader noted.
Russian standard in Rotterdam was briefly offered at a discount of $40-$45 on Monday when the backwardation was at its widest, compared to a $10-$20 discount previously, he said.
"But it won't be offered like that anymore," a trader added.
The tightness was causing discomfort for customers, most of whom operate hand to mouth, one trader said. It was also being exacerbated by late deliveries by contractors.
"Everyone's been too focused on terminal markets to be too worried about physical business. The physical market is tight and there's very little copper being transacted," a trader said.
However, he reported UK grade A traded at a premium to LME cash metal of close to $50.
Analysts said it remained to be seen whether the market could see more liquidity in the next few weeks.

"The big question for the market is whether the unwinding of the spreads on Monday will lead to the apperance of more metal into the market over the next few weeks which may have been 'white lined'", brokers GNI said in a report.
"In addition it is likely that the very high levels of backwardation will have attracted physical supplies to the LME as well."
